Package IoTFleetManagement.user.controller

Klasse AuthController

java.lang.Object
IoTFleetManagement.user.controller.AuthController
@RestController @RequestMapping("/auth") public class AuthController extends Object
Controller responsible for handling user authentication and registration requests.

Provides REST endpoints for user login, registration, and retrieving user-specific agents.

Autor:
Lara, Jasmin1707, streitwies

  • Methodendetails

    • login

      @PostMapping("/login") public org.springframework.http.ResponseEntity<String> login(jakarta.servlet.http.HttpServletRequest request, @RequestParam("username") String username, @RequestParam("password") String password)
      Authenticates a user based on provided credentials.

      On successful authentication, it initializes a security context and associates it with the current session.

      Parameter:
      request - the HTTP request object
      username - the username of the user attempting to log in
      password - the password of the user attempting to log in
      Gibt zurück:
      a ResponseEntity containing a success message if authentication is successful, or an unauthorized response if credentials are invalid

    • register

      @PostMapping("/register") public org.springframework.http.ResponseEntity<?> register(@RequestParam("email") String email, @RequestParam("username") String username, @RequestParam("password") String password)
      Registers a new user with the default "ROLE_USER" role.

      Validates if the role exists and checks for unique username and email before creating a new user.

      Parameter:
      email - the email of the user to be registered
      username - the username of the user to be registered
      password - the password of the user to be registered
      Gibt zurück:
      a ResponseEntity containing the newly created user if registration is successful, or an error message if the username, email, or role is invalid

    • registerAdmin

      @PostMapping("/register-admin") public org.springframework.http.ResponseEntity<?> registerAdmin(@RequestParam("email") String email, @RequestParam("username") String username, @RequestParam("password") String password, @RequestParam("invitationToken") String invitationToken)
      Endpoint to register a new admin user with the "ROLE_ADMIN" role.

      This endpoint allows a user to register as an admin by providing their email, username, password, and a valid invitation token. The invitation token ensures that only authorized users can register as admins.

      Example Usage:

       // Example cURL command to register a new admin
 curl -X POST \
      https://localhost:8443/auth/register-admin \
      -H "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \
      -d "email=newadmin@example.com" \
      -d "username=newAdmin" \
      -d "password=SecurePassword123" \
      -d "invitationToken=ABC123XYZ" \
      -k
      Parameter:
      email - The email address of the new admin. Must be unique.
      username - The username of the new admin. Must be unique.
      password - The password for the new admin.
      invitationToken - A valid invitation token for admin registration.
      Gibt zurück:
      A ResponseEntity containing:
      • The created admin user if successful (HTTP 201).
      • An error message if the token is invalid, expired, or the input parameters are invalid (HTTP 400 or 403).
      • An error message if the email or username is already in use (HTTP 409).
      Löst aus:
      AlreadyExistsException - If the email or username is already taken.

    • checkAuthentication

      @GetMapping("/check") public org.springframework.http.ResponseEntity<?> checkAuthentication()
      This endpoint verifies if a user is currently authenticated by checking the SecurityContext for valid authentication details. If the user is not authenticated, it returns an HTTP 401 Unauthorized status. If the user is authenticated, it returns an HTTP 200 OK status.
      Gibt zurück:
      a ResponseEntity representing the authentication status: - HTTP 200 OK if the user is authenticated. - HTTP 401 Unauthorized if the user is not authenticated.

    • logout

      @PostMapping("/logout") public org.springframework.http.ResponseEntity<?> logout(jakarta.servlet.http.HttpServletRequest request, jakarta.servlet.http.HttpServletResponse response)
      This endpoint is responsible for logging out the currently authenticated user. It invalidates the user's session and clears any authentication details from the SecurityContext. If a user is authenticated, their session will be ended, and a successful logout response will be returned.
      Parameter:
      request - the HttpServletRequest that represents the HTTP request, which is used to access the current session for logout purposes
      response - the HttpServletResponse that represents the HTTP response, used to send the result of the logout operation to the client
      Gibt zurück:
      a ResponseEntity representing the result of the logout operation: - HTTP 200 OK with a success message if the user was logged out successfully.

    • getUserAgents

      @GetMapping("/user/agents") public org.springframework.http.ResponseEntity<List<Agent>> getUserAgents()
      This endpoint retrieves the agents associated with the currently authenticated user. It checks the SecurityContext to verify if the user is authenticated to perform the operation. If the user is authenticated, the endpoint returns a list of agents registered under the user's account. If the user is not authenticated, it returns an HTTP 401 Unauthorized status.
      Gibt zurück:
      a ResponseEntity containing: - HTTP 200 OK with a list of Agent objects if the user is authenticated and agents are found. - HTTP 401 Unauthorized if the user is not authenticated.
